title: Mongol Khanate
capsule: The Mongol Khanate — effectively the Northern Yuan dynasty and its steppe successor polities — survived after the Ming dynasty expelled the Yuan court from China in 1368, retreating to the Mongolian Plateau where Toghon Temur and his descendants maintained Chinggisid legitimacy. The polity fragmented repeatedly: the Oirat federation under Esen Taishi dominated in the mid-fifteenth century, capturing the Ming Zhengtong Emperor at the Tumu Crisis of 1449, before eastern Mongol khans reasserted control under Dayan Khan (r. c. 1479–1517), who reunified the Mongolian tribes and divided them among his sons. The Mongol Khanate's autonomous steppe existence effectively ended when the Qing dynasty systematically incorporated the eastern Mongol leagues through the Banner system by 1635 and subjugated the western Oirats (Dzungars) across the following century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent of the post-Yuan Mongol steppe polities is largely conjectural, based on textual references to tribal grazing ranges and campaign narratives; precise boundaries are not inscriptionally attested and reconstruction varies significantly among scholars.
